sections.heading: Standard Families Recap
bullets: 17000 family — conformity assessment (17000 vocabulary, 17020 inspection, 17021 certification bodies, 17025 testing/calibration labs).

sections.heading: Organizations Recap
bullets: ISO — international standard-writer, founded 1947, HQ Geneva, members are national standards bodies.
IEC — electrical/electronic standards, founded 1906, co-publishes with ISO where scopes overlap (17025, 27001).
ITU — telecom standards, founded 1865, a UN specialized agency (unlike ISO/IEC).
BIS — India's national standards body, adapts ISO/IEC standards, HQ New Delhi.
NABCB — accredits India's management-system certification bodies.

sections.heading: Terminology Recap
bullets: Standard vs Technical Specification — a standard requires full consensus; a technical specification does not (used for emerging areas).
Conformity — actually meeting a standard's requirements.
Certification — third-party confirmation an organization conforms.
Accreditation — confirmation that a certification/testing body is itself competent.
Audit — a systematic check of whether a system actually follows what it claims to follow.
Management system — the interrelated policies/processes an organization uses to run toward its objectives.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: This is the compiled reference sheet for every ISO standard number, organization, and term covered across the ISO subject.
keyFacts: 17000 family = conformity assessment; 9000 family = quality; 14000 family = environment; 45000 family = OH&S.
commonConfusion: Guidance documents (9004, 31000, 19011, 10001, 10002) are the ones most often mistakenly described as 'certifiable' — they are not.

highYieldFacts: The master table above is the single highest-yield reference page in the ISO subject — headquarters/founding-year facts for the parent organizations, and certifiable-vs-not status for every standard, in one place.
17000-family standards (17020, 17021, 17025) each govern a different type of conformity-assessment BODY — inspection, certification, and laboratory testing respectively.
ISO/IEC co-publishes standards only where scope crosses into electrical/electronic/technology territory (17025, 27001) — most ISO standards (9001, 14001, 45001, 22000, 15189) are ISO-only.
commonTraps: Do not assume every standard number in this list is certifiable — check the table's 'Certifiable?' column before answering.
Do not forget that ISO/IEC 17025 and ISO/IEC 27001 carry the 'ISO/IEC' prefix specifically because IEC co-publishes them.
mustRemember: When a question gives you a standard number you don't recognise, first ask: quality (9xxx), environment (14xxx), safety (45xxx), or conformity assessment (17xxx)? — the number range itself is a strong clue.
The four-layer chain — standard → certification → accreditation → regulation — resolves most remaining confusion.
